assessment.reason: The article develops a conceptual checklist for item selection in preference-based measures. Measurement and suitability for health-state valuation are primary, but no EQ instrument or EuroQol method is the primary research object. The EuroQol Research Foundation explicitly funded the work.

studies.label: Development of item-selection criteria for preference-based measures used in economic evaluation
studies.family_rationale: The principal contribution is a structured checklist of 22 criteria that classifies the considerations needed when selecting items for preference-based measures. The paper discusses method quality, but its main output is the conceptual checklist.

items.label: Criteria for selecting items for preference-based measures

items.statement: The authors present criteria covering 22 aspects of item selection for preference-based measures.
Criteria 1–12 address general questionnaire design, criteria 13–19 have increased importance for preference-based measures, and criteria 20–22 address requirements specific to valuation.

values.subgroup: Criteria with greater importance for preference-based measures

source: Full article, Item selection criteria for a measure of QoL which will be valued based on public preferences, paragraph 3

items.statement: The valuation-specific criteria require important and tradable domains, items that do not attribute a problem to a circumstance, and response options that have a consistent direction.
source: Full article, Ensure items are suitable for measuring QALYs, final six paragraphs

items.statement: Applying the criteria during item selection can limit problems at the later valuation stage.
Application should be iterative and should use evidence from people who will complete the measure and people whose preferences will be elicited.
source: Full article, Item selection criteria for a measure of QoL which will be valued based on public preferences, paragraph 3

items.statement: The criteria can conflict, so development teams must make judgments about their application.
source: Full article, Accuracy and completion, discussion of criterion 7

items.statement: Whether valuation respondents will trade improvements in one item against other domains can be difficult to establish before valuation exercises are conducted.
source: Full article, Ensure items are suitable for measuring QALYs, paragraph beginning ‘Criteria 20–22’

items.label: Criteria for item selection for preference-based measures

items.exact_state: Criteria covering 22 aspects were developed and presented.

items.label: Valuation suitability of items
items.description: Items in a preference-based measure must support comprehensible health-state valuation and meaningful trade-offs across domains and against length of life.

items.label: Interpersonal and intertemporal comparability
items.description: Items used to calculate QALYs should describe the specified current period without depending on comparisons with other people, expectations, or other periods.
source: Full article, Ensure items are suitable for measuring QALYs, paragraphs discussing criteria 14–19
